title: Inadequacies of Large Language Model Benchmarks in the Era of Generative Artificial Intelligence

bias_targets.methodology: Structured literature review and thematic analysis evaluating the predominantly English-centric nature of 23 LLM benchmarks and their failure to account for linguistic variability and embedded logic diversity across different languages.

Thematic analysis of benchmark datasets and rubrics to assess their reliance on standardized answers that impose specific cultural, social, political, religious, and ideological norms, thereby neglecting global pluralism.

Systematic critique of benchmark construction and assessment processes, examining how subjective biases are introduced by non-diverse human curators and how inherent biases are amplified when using LLMs to generate evaluations or act as judges.
